Baltimore expands secure AI pilot

By Ada Reporter

The reported development expands a secure artificial-intelligence pilot across several Baltimore public services. Officials said the work will be evaluated against published reliability and privacy criteria before any broader deployment.

The city released procurement and oversight documents alongside the announcement. Independent researchers will review the pilot, and the evaluation plan calls for public reporting of material failures.

Community representatives asked for clearer appeal procedures and stronger limits on data retention. Officials said those questions will be addressed before the first operational trial begins.

The initiative remains limited in scope, and the agencies involved emphasized that the pilot does not authorize autonomous decisions.
